definition: time-to-collision with the hazard when the request is issued
context: D003: fixed; literature: varied 4-10 s (literature matrix L001/L002/L007)
reported_value_or_rule: D003: 7 s before collision (TTC-triggered); multi-TOR values in 26 trials (B1)
notes: Design choice of the system / experiment, not a physical constant.

element: human takeover time (interface to layer B)
definition: time from TOR to a takeover action (definition varies by study)
reported_value_or_rule: mean 2.72 s (SD 1.45) between studies; strongly associated with time budget (r = 0.73)
notes: Depends on the time budget itself, so TOT is not independent of T_TOR.

element: regulatory timing of MRM after a transition demand
quantity: earliest MRM start without driver response
definition: time after the start of a transition demand before an MRM may start if the driver has not deactivated the system
reported_value_or_rule: R157 §5.4.4.1: MRM 'shall be started, earliest 10 s after the start of the transition demand' if the driver does not deactivate; §5.4.4.1.1: immediately on severe ALKS/vehicle failure; §5.4.3.2: escalation at the latest 4 s after the start; §5.4.4: the demand ends only at deactivation or MRM start; §2.3: transition phase = duration of the transition demand
observable_in_D003: NO (D003 is not an R157 system)
notes: Correction (R3B-0): '10 s transition period' was an oversimplification. The regulation sets an earliest MRM start of 10 s; the transition phase has no fixed length and ends at deactivation or MRM start. It is not a takeover-time requirement.

quantity: automation behaviour between TOR and effective human control
definition: whether and how automation keeps lateral / longitudinal control after the request
evidence_kind: regulation (official text); simulation model; project observation
context: R157 §5.4.3 (both series): during the transition phase the system 'shall continue to operate' and may reduce speed but not bring the vehicle to standstill unless required by the situation; SUMO/TransAID preparatory phase
reported_value_or_rule: R157 rule; SUMO behaviour; D003 cell-specific actuator changes at TOR (B17)
notes: This is the main source of automation-commanded a_pre (headway enlargement = deceleration).

quantity: time when a control channel becomes human-authoritative
definition: moment the human's input takes priority on a channel (override / deactivation)
context: R157 §6.2.5.2: during a transition demand the system shall only be deactivated by (a) a steering override while holding the steering control or a brake/accelerator override while holding it (§6.2.5.1), or (b) detection that the driver holds the steering control and is attentive (§6.3.1.1). §6.3.2: braking overrides longitudinal control only if it yields higher deceleration than the system; §6.3.3: accelerator input may override; §6.3.1: steering override needs force and duration thresholds. D003: mode-switch button (Manual_Start).
reported_value_or_rule: for R157 systems: conditional, per-channel, threshold-based; for D003: not identified
observable_in_D003: NO (Manual_Start authority UNRESOLVED, B7; channels not driver-only, B17)
notes: Authority transfer is channel-specific and conditional on holding the steering control; it is not TOR and not a button press by definition. Code assumes T_authority = TOR.

quantity: time of first effective human input on the relevant channel
definition: first human input that changes vehicle motion
notes: Distinct from TOR, from Manual_Start and from authority transfer.

definition: both agents act on the same control channel with arbitration
notes: Conceptual layer element; no parameterisation available.

definition: automation releases propulsion / control at TOR without continued support
context: R157 §5.4.3 requires continued operation during the transition phase, so immediate release is not R157-compliant behaviour
observable_in_D003: UNKNOWN (possibly in some D003 cells; B17)
notes: Retained as a counterfactual bound, not a representative policy.

definition: deceleration applied by the system when the human does not take over
evidence_kind: regulation (official text); software default; standard scope
context: R157 in-lane MRM; SUMO default; ISO 23793-1 types
reported_value_or_rule: R157 Rev.1 §5.5.2 (00 series §5.5.1): slowed down 'with an aim of achieving a deceleration demand not greater than 4.0 m/s2'; higher demand permissible for very short durations (e.g. haptic warning) or on severe failure. Rev.1 §5.5.1: stop in a target stop area, with MRM lane change if capable. SUMO default mrmDecel 1.5 m/s2 (software). ISO 23793-1 numbers not accessed.
notes: Correction (R3B-0): 4.0 m/s2 is a design aim for the deceleration demand, not a hard maximum of achieved deceleration.

definition: time after the transition demand at which the system begins the MRM
reported_value_or_rule: R157 §5.4.4.1 / §5.4.4.1.1 (see T03); SUMO: after the ToC lead time

definition: system-initiated manoeuvre on imminent collision risk to avoid / mitigate
reported_value_or_rule: §2.6: imminent collision risk = collision not avoidable with a braking demand below 5 m/s2; §5.3.1.1: any system deceleration demand above 5.0 m/s2 is an emergency manoeuvre; §5.3.2: up to full braking and/or evasive manoeuvre within the lane; §6.2.5.3: deactivation may be delayed during an EM
notes: During an EM the system may retain authority (deactivation may be delayed): a competing event for human fallback.

definition: deceleration / jerk limits of automation in normal operation
reported_value_or_rule: ISO 15622 about 3.5 m/s2 / 2.5 m/s3 (SECONDARY ONLY); for R157 systems any demand above 5.0 m/s2 is an EM (§5.3.1.1)
notes: Bounds automation-commanded a_pre during continued support (V20).

reported_value_or_rule: D003 = mandatory, automation-initiated, driver in control after (plus protocol handback)

definition: what the D003 automation did at and after TOR
reported_value_or_rule: accelerator/brake/steering channel changes within 0.3 s of TOR in 6 of 9 cells (B17); not described by owners

definition: model state of driver capability after resuming control
notes: Model assumption without empirical anchor in sources checked.

quantity: safe time budget vs time to control
definition: prior framework comparing available time (safe TTC) with takeover time plus manoeuvre execution time
context: authority transitions (CACC/ACC deactivation) in traffic simulation
reported_value_or_rule: Delta TC = STB - TC; conflict threshold 0.9 s; virtual crash < 0
observable_in_D003: NO (TOT and t_action not separable in D003; B17)
notes: Closest prior art for T_available >= T_required; action time taken from simulation traces, not closed form.
